note: TWO VINTAGES IN THIS TABLE. (A) The 9 non-single-family districts below (TF, TH, MF-1, MF-2, CN, C-1, C-3, OF, IN) are unchanged from the currently-governing code and use the ORIGINAL note that follows. (B) The 4 single-family districts (RE, RT, RS, RM) were replaced 2026-09-07 with data from Georgetown's adopted-but-not-yet-effective UDC rewrite (City Council adopted 2026-08-11; effective 2026-11-01 per rewrite Section 1.09) -- these are primary-source-verified against the rewrite PDF, not against the real code-section atom corpus, because that corpus only contains the CURRENTLY-in-force (pre-rewrite) text (confirmed live: zero real atoms mention the rewrite's new district name 'Residential Traditional', while several mention the pre-rewrite name 'Residential Low Density') -- there is nothing in the real corpus to round-trip rewrite text against. FOLLOW-UP NEEDED (not done here): once the rewrite is closer to taking effect or after 2026-11-01, the other 9 districts need the same post-rewrite research the 4 SF ones just got, or this table carries two vintages indefinitely. See each district's own provenance for adopted_date/effective_date/pre_rewrite_value_verified fields marking which vintage a given value belongs to. --- ORIGINAL NOTE (districts TF/TH/MF-1/MF-2/CN/C-1/C-3/OF/IN, current code): Codified from the City of Georgetown Unified Development Code (UDC), Chapter 6 (Residential Development Standards) Section 6.02 and Chapter 7 (Non-Residential Development Standards) Table 7.02.020 — Supplement 15, codified through Ordinance No. 2025-54 adopted September 9, 2025 (Municode ProductID 13943, job Id 480427). Source is Municode; each district cites its own Section 6.02.0x0 (residential) or the shared Table 7.02.020 (non-residential) deep-link. PENDING REWRITE CAVEAT: Georgetown's UDC is mid-rewrite with an updated version expected ~mid-2026; this table pins the CURRENT IN-FORCE edition (Supp. 15 / Ord. 2025-54) and MUST be re-verified when the rewrite lands. MODELING NOTES: (1) The Georgetown UDC dimensional tables state 'Impervious Cover, maximum %: See Section 11.02' (residential) / 'Impervious coverage: Refer to Section 11.02' (non-residential) and state NO per-district building lot-coverage cap, so both max_impervious_pct and max_lot_coverage_pct are flagged not_specified in provenance and carry 100 as a non-binding stand-in (the envelope draw uses setbacks, not these fields). (2) The UDC's corner/street-facing value is 'Side/Rear Street Setback' — codified as side_corner_ft. (3) Residential 'Side Setback' is the base interior side; the MF-1/MF-2 larger side/rear values are the setback-to-residential-district figures and are NOT used as the base side_ft (base interior side is codified). (4) TH (Townhouse) side_ft uses the 'Non-shared Wall Side Setback' (10 ft); the shared-wall side is 0. (5) Non-residential districts (CN/C-1/C-3/OF/BP/IN/PF) draw from the single shared Table 7.02.020; side_ft is the base 'Side setback, min.' and side_corner_ft mirrors that base where the table states no distinct corner value (non-res table has no separate street-side column, so side_corner_ft = side_ft, flagged). (6) AG (Agriculture) and MU-DT/MU (form-based, 'See Section 4.09') are EXCLUDED — no simple per-district front/side/rear setback table. --- REWRITE RESEARCH NOTE (districts RE/RT/RS/RM, effective 2026-11-01): IMPORTANT TIMING CAVEAT: Georgetown's original UDC (adopted 2003-03-11, in force today) is being wholesale replaced. City Council adopted a full UDC rewrite on 2026-08-11; per UDC Section 1.09 the rewrite becomes effective 2026-11-01. This file is coded from the REWRITE text (City of Georgetown, 'Unified Development Code 2026', PDF published at https://cms3.revize.com/revize/georgetowntx/Documents/Development%20Services/Planning/Unified%20Development%20Code/UDC%20Rewrite%20Draft%20Content/Unified%20Development%20Code%208.11.2026.pdf, accessed 2026-09-06), NOT from the pre-rewrite code that is the only code legally in force between now and 2026-10-31. The rewrite's own Section 4.02 'Zoning District Equivalency Table' confirms these are direct successors of the pre-rewrite districts, same short codes, same lineage: pre-rewrite 'RE Residential Estate'->RE (unchanged), 'RL Residential Low Density'->RT Residential Traditional, 'RS Residential Single-family'->RS Residential Suburban, 'TF Two-family'/'TH Townhouse'->RM Residential Mix. Max building height for RS is independently cross-checked at 35 ft under BOTH codes via a City of Georgetown Planning Department staff report (Sofia Nelson, Planning Director; City Council item, 2026-01-14, https://d2kbkoa27fdvtw.cloudfront.net/georgetown/e60a6c7d2d185c1f926d7bba471eb3350.pdf, 'Current UDC' height table, RS = 35'), which is the only pre-rewrite dimensional figure this pass could independently verify -- the pre-rewrite code's front/side/rear/corner setback and impervious-cover numbers could NOT be verified (see confidence report; Municode's current-UDC pages at https://library.municode.com/tx/georgetown/codes/unified_development_code render client-side via an Angular SPA that returned only an empty app shell to every fetch method available this session, including a browser-UA curl GET (HTTP 200, 6KB shell, zero table content) and the Wayback Machine's historical crawls of the same URL pattern (all captures 1.8-3.3KB, same shell, per CDX API query), so no pre-rewrite chapter text was retrievable this session). SCOPE: covers the rewrite's four Chapter 7 residential districts whose descriptions explicitly allow single-family detached and/or attached housing -- RE Residential Estate (Sec. 7.02.030), RT Residential Traditional (Sec. 7.02.040), RS Residential Suburban (Sec. 7.02.050, the City's standard single-family-detached district and the direct successor to pre-rewrite 'RS'), and RM Residential Mix (Sec. 7.02.060, allows single-family detached/attached alongside duplex/townhouse). OMITTED as out of scope for a single-family corpus: AG Agriculture, MF-1/MF-2 multifamily, MH Manufactured Housing, all non-residential and overlay districts, and all ETJ-specific standards. Where a district's Chapter 7 table splits values by garage/parking access (front-loaded vs. alley-loaded lots), this file reports the front-loaded ('front-access') column as the canonical row, since front-loaded is the default/majority lot configuration; alley-loaded variants are captured in each field's provenance quote and are NOT separately rowed (schema is one row per district). Georgetown's 2026 code has no 'lot coverage' concept distinct from impervious cover (full-text search for 'lot coverage'/'building coverage' in the 501-page rewrite returned zero hits) -- max_lot_coverage_pct uses the same non-binding sentinel-100 convention established in this corpus's pflugerville-tx.json for a genuinely absent metric. max_impervious_pct values for RE and RT carry lower confidence: Table 13.02.010-2 (p.320) labels every row with a 'front-access'/'alley-access' qualifier, but RE's and RT's own Chapter 7 dimensional tables have no alley-loaded lot type at all, so the qualifier attached to their single impervious-cover row in Table 13.02.010-2 is very likely a pdftotext column-bleed artifact from the neighboring RS/RM rows -- the numeric value (RE 20%, RT 40%) is transcribed exactly as printed and directly adjacent to the correct district name, but the access-type label should not be trusted. See per-field provenance for full detail and the accompanying sourcing/confidence note delivered alongside this file.
